## 33fcd12e6b89

**Reproduced shortcut: fixed-shape recognition.** The assigned generator hash is
`428603f00288561e66155c0932b142ea02571ac508e68caa2b6c2d803755e43a`;
the canonical rule hash is `4151627dc5c7`. The target was not modified.

The sampler emits only three hard-coded normalized object shapes. A plausible
rival is:

> Apply the correct marker-3-to-marker-4 translation only when the remaining
> object has one of those three normalized shapes; otherwise leave the input
>unchanged.

That rival fits both canonical training demonstrations and all 600 generated
samples checked across default/easy/medium/hard, with zero mismatches. The sampler
never emitted the 2×2-square shape below.

Exact 9×9 counterexample input:

```text
000000000
030000000
000000000
000040000
066000000
066000000
000000000
000000000
000000000
```

It has one color-3 marker at `(1,1)`, one color-4 marker at `(3,4)`, and a
connected monochrome 2×2 object at rows 4–5, columns 1–2. The guide vector is
`(+2,+3)`, so the intended rule moves the square to rows 6–7, columns 4–5 while
retaining the markers. The fixed-shape rival leaves the original square in place.

The current generator’s `self_check` returns `[]`. The input also satisfies every
documented invariant used by the audit probe: 9×9 is inside the advertised axis
bounds, markers are unique, the object is nonempty and connected, the translated
object is in bounds, and it avoids both markers. Thus this is a documented-domain
member accepted by the validator, not merely a malformed negative fixture.

Racket was executed from `repo` with:

```text
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 33fcd12e6b89 \
  --input ../checks/audit/33fcd12e6b89/input.json \
  --out ../checks/audit/33fcd12e6b89/racket.json
```

Exit status was 0. Full input, actual Racket output, rival output, hashes, domain
checks, canonical-fit results, and 600-sample support measurements are retained in:

- `checks/audit/33fcd12e6b89/input.json`
- `checks/audit/33fcd12e6b89/racket.json`
- `checks/audit/33fcd12e6b89/rival.json`
- `checks/audit/33fcd12e6b89/probe.json`
- `checks/audit/33fcd12e6b89/probe.py`

No fix was applied because this was an audit-only target. A future repair should
replace the three fixed templates with a constructive family of connected shapes,
add an observable shape-size/complexity control, strengthen `self_check` to enforce
the stated geometry, and declare this fixed-shape rival as a semantic competitor.
